claims.text: A Pulumi blog post titled 'SST Runs on the Pulumi Engine: What It Means to Build on Pulumi' exists at /blog/sst-built-on-pulumi/ and covers the engine mechanics behind SST's migration to Pulumi.
AWS CDK tied infrastructure to AWS, making multi-cloud nearly impossible for SST, and SST was originally built on top of AWS CDK which let developers define infrastructure using TypeScript or Python.
AWS CDK supports only TypeScript and Python, while Pulumi supports any programming language.
Pulumi supports AWS, Azure, GCP, and on-prem while AWS CDK is AWS-only.
Pulumi deployments are faster than AWS CDK deployments because CloudFormation is slower than direct execution.
AWS CDK supports only AWS Secrets Manager for secrets management, while Pulumi supports cross-cloud secrets.
Pulumi lets you define infrastructure in TypeScript, Python, Go, or C# and deploy to AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and on-premises environments.
Ion is the code name for SST's new deployment engine, deploying components via Pulumi instead of CDK and CloudFormation, and will be released as SST v3 once stable.
SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for its providers and deployment engine and bridges Terraform providers through Pulumi.
SST makes money primarily through its managed service SST Console, which is optional and includes a free tier.

A Founding Engineer at SST said: 'With Pulumi, the deployment process feels like a natural extension of writing code - it's intuitive and powerful and capable of advanced things that traditional IaC tools can't handle.'
SST v3 replaced AWS CDK and CloudFormation with an embedded Pulumi engine that calls Terraform-bridged providers to make the underlying cloud API calls.
Running `sst deploy` requires no separate Pulumi install and no Pulumi account or Pulumi Cloud dependency; the engine ships inside the SST CLI.
SST v3 keeps deployment state in an S3 bucket in the user's own AWS account rather than in Pulumi Cloud.
Nitric and Defang also run application deployments through the Pulumi engine rather than building their own diff, state, and provider layer.
SST is still shipping and the SST team's public attention has broadened to include opencode, an AI coding agent.
SST is an open source TypeScript framework from the team formerly known as Serverless Stack, for deploying full-stack applications to AWS and more than 150 other providers.
SST apps define infrastructure and code together in a single `sst.config.ts` file using SST's own components.
Through 2023 SST's provisioning layer was built on AWS CDK and CloudFormation; in late 2023 the team began a rewrite code-named Ion.
Ion shipped as SST v3 in mid-2024 and has been the only supported SST architecture since.

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'Ion is a code name for a new engine for deploying SST applications. The constructs (or components) are defined using Terraform providers and deployed using Pulumi; as opposed to CDK and CloudFormation (CFN).'

SST's blog post 'Moving away from CDK' says: 'When you run `sst deploy`, those resources make a call to an embedded Pulumi engine that makes a call to their bridged Terraform provider, and this makes the AWS SDK calls to create your resources.'
SST docs 'What is SST' say: 'SST uses Pulumi behind the scenes for the providers and the deployment engine. And Terraform's providers are bridged through Pulumi.'
Gautier Blandin's article 'Terraform, Pulumi, SST: a tradeoff analysis' says SST uses the Pulumi engine under the hood and lets users write Pulumi code in addition to SST constructs.
Kiryl Anoshka's dev.to article says: 'You may notice right away the imports from Pulumi. It means the whole deployment process will be built on Pulumi now.'

SST's platform/package.json depends on @pulumi/pulumi plus @pulumi/aws, @pulumi/cloudflare, @pulumi/command, @pulumi/docker-build, @pulumi/random, @pulumi/tls and @pulumiverse/vercel as direct dependencies, in the anomalyco/sst repository (formerly sst/sst).
The Pulumi engine diffs desired vs. actual state, builds a dependency graph and orders operations; Pulumi's Terraform bridge translates resources into cloud API calls.
Pulumi's Terraform bridge (pulumi-terraform-bridge) is Apache-2.0 licensed.
Pulumi's engine does not require a Pulumi account, a network call to Pulumi Cloud, or any Pulumi-hosted service to run.
Pulumi's Automation API lets teams embed Pulumi programs inside their own tools.
The Pulumi provider bridge lets any Pulumi user consume Terraform providers directly.
AWS alone exposes hundreds of resource types.
Nitric's docs state that 'all of the direct deployment providers use Pulumi under the hood for their deployments', with official Nitric providers built on Pulumi's AWS, GCP, and Azure providers.
Defang's pulumi-defang provider takes a Compose file, translates it to a Pulumi program, and runs `pulumi up`.
Resources without a dedicated SST construct can be defined directly in Pulumi and deployed as part of the same SST app.
The latest SST release, v4.17.1, went out in July 2026.
The `sst` npm package gets roughly 796,000 downloads a week (796,291 for September 5-11, 2026).
SST's team page credits the same team behind opencode, an open source AI coding agent, and opencode now has more GitHub stars than SST.
SST does not invoke the Terraform CLI or write Terraform state.
If you run SST, you are running Pulumi's engine.
Pulumi Cloud, policy as code, and components provide cross-team visibility, central guardrails, and shared infrastructure patterns, and none require leaving the engine SST uses.
SST is a strong fit for an opinionated full-stack application framework.
